title.zh: 卷443 列傳二百三十 孙家鼐 张百熙 唐景崇 於式枚 沈家本
title.en: Volume 443 Biographies 230: Sun Jianai, Zhang Baixi, Tang Jingchong, Yu Shimei, Shen Jiaben
title.raw: 卷443 列傳二百三十 孙家鼐 张百熙 唐景崇 於式枚 沈家本

sentences.zh: 孫家鼐，字燮臣，安徽壽州人。

translations.literal: Sun Jianai, style name Xiecheng, was a man of Shouzhou, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jianai, whose style was Xiecheng, came from Shouzhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he was jinshi, first in the first class, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 9 he topped the first class of jinshi graduates and was made a Compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷侍讀，入直上書房。

translations.literal: He successively served as Reader-in-Waiting and entered service in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the post of Reader-in-Waiting and joined the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，命在毓慶宮行走，與尚書翁同龢授上讀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he was ordered to serve in the Palace of Cherished Growth, and together with Minister Weng Tonghe instructed the heir apparent in reading.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 4 he was assigned to the Palace of Cherished Growth, where he and Minister Weng Tonghe tutored the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became a Grand Secretariat academician and was elevated to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to Grand Secretariat academician and then Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 江西學政陳寶琛疏請以先儒黃宗羲、顧炎武從祀文廟，議者多以爲未可，家鼐與潘祖蔭、翁同龢、孫詒經等再請，始議准。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Education Commissioner Chen Baochen memorialized asking that the former Confucians Huang Zongxi and Gu Yanwu be granted accompanying sacrifice in the Temple of Confucius; many in the deliberation held it inadvisable; Jianai, together with Pan Zuyin, Weng Tonghe, Sun Yijing, and others petitioned again, and only then was approval granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi education commissioner Chen Baochen asked that Huang Zongxi and Gu Yanwu be enshrined in the Confucian temple, most officials objected; Jianai joined Pan Zuyin, Weng Tonghe, Sun Yijing, and others in pressing the request again until it was approved.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授都察院左都御史、工部尚書，兼順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and Minister of Works, and concurrently Metropolitan Magistrate of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of Works, while also serving as Shuntian metropolitan magistrate.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中日事起，朝議主戰，家鼐力言釁不可啓。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year trouble arose between China and Japan; court opinion favored war; Jianai strenuously argued that conflict must not be provoked.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-Japanese crisis broke out in the twentieth year, the court leaned toward war, but Jianai insisted that hostilities must not be opened.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, as Minister of Personnel he was made assisting Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he became assisting Grand Secretary while retaining the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 命爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as Superintendent of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed in charge of education as Superintendent of Education.

sentences.zh: 時方議變法，廢科舉，興學校，設報編書，皆特交核覆，家鼐一裁以正。

translations.literal: At that time reform was under discussion—the abolition of the civil service examinations, establishment of schools, founding of newspapers, compilation of books—all were specially referred to him for examination and approval, and Jianai settled each matter with rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: As the court debated abolishing the examinations, founding schools, launching newspapers, and commissioning new books, each proposal was sent to him for review, and he judged every one on its merits.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏謂：「國家廣集卿士以資議政，聽言固不厭求詳，然執兩用中，精擇審處，尤賴聖知。

translations.literal: He once memorialized, saying: "The state broadly gathers high ministers to supply deliberation on government; in hearing words one indeed does not tire of seeking detail, yet holding the two and using the mean, finely choosing and carefully disposing—all the more rely on sacred wisdom."
translations.idiomatic: In one memorial he wrote: "The state gathers eminent ministers to deliberate on policy, and it is right to hear every argument in full; yet to hold competing views in balance, choose wisely, and decide carefully depends above all on the emperor's discernment."

sentences.zh: 」其所建議，類能持大體。

translations.literal: " His proposals in general were able to uphold the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: His recommendations, as a rule, kept sight of the larger interest of the state.

sentences.zh: 及議廢立，家鼐獨持不可。

translations.literal: When the question of deposing and enthroning arose, Jianai alone held it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated deposing and replacing the emperor, he alone opposed the move.

sentences.zh: 旋以病乞罷。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he asked to retire on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sought retirement, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，乘輿西狩，召赴行在，起禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the imperial carriage went west on campaign, he was summoned to the traveling court and reappointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, after the court fled west, he was called to the traveling palace and restored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 還京，拜體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: After the return to Beijing he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 歷轉東閣、文淵閣，晉武英殿。

translations.literal: He successively transferred through the Eastern Pavilion and Literary Deep Pavilion, and was advanced to the Martial Eminence Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from the Eastern and Literary Deep pavilions up to the Martial Eminence Hall.

sentences.zh: 充學務大臣，裁度規章，折衷中外，嚴定宗旨，一以敦行實學爲主，學風爲之一靖。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Education, measured regulations, balanced Chinese and foreign, strictly fixed the guiding principle, taking throughout the promotion of practical learning as the main thing; academic style thereby became calm.
translations.idiomatic: As Minister of Education he drafted regulations that balanced Chinese and Western learning, set a firm course centered on practical study, and brought the schools back under control.

sentences.zh: 議改官制，命與慶親王奕劻、軍機大臣瞿鴻禨總司核定。

translations.literal: When reform of the official system was discussed, he was ordered together with Prince Qing Yikuang and Grand Councillor Qu Hongji to take overall charge of examination and approval.
translations.idiomatic: During the debate over bureaucratic reform he was ordered, together with Prince Qing Yikuang and Grand Councillor Qu Hongji, to oversee the final review.

sentences.zh: 御史趙啓霖劾奕劻及其子貝子載振受賄納優，命醇親王載灃與家鼐往按，啓霖坐汚衊親貴褫職，而載振尋亦乞罷兼官。

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Qilin impeached Yikuang and his son Beile Zai Zhen for accepting bribes and hiring entertainers; Zaifeng, Prince Chun, and Jianai were ordered to go investigate; Qilin was punished for slandering the imperial kin and dismissed from office, while Zai Zhen soon also asked to resign his concurrent posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Zhao Qilin accused Yikuang and his son Beile Zai Zhen of bribery and keeping actors, Prince Chun Zaifeng and Jianai were sent to investigate; Qilin was stripped of office for defaming the imperial clan, and Zai Zhen soon resigned his extra posts as well.

sentences.zh: 資政院立，命貝子溥倫及家鼐爲總裁，一持正議不阿。

translations.literal: When the Political Consultative Council was established, Beile Pulun and Jianai were ordered to serve as presidents; he consistently upheld upright opinion and did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: When the Political Consultative Council was founded, he and Beile Pulun were named its presidents, and he refused to trim his views to please anyone.

sentences.zh: 時詔諸臣輪班進講，家鼐撰尚書四子書講義以進。

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered ministers in rotation to advance and lecture; Jianai composed lecture texts on the Documents, the Four Books, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne ordered ministers to lecture in turn, he prepared commentaries on the Documents and the Four Books and presented them.

sentences.zh: 三十四年二月，以鄉舉重逢，賞太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year, on the occasion of the provincial examination cycle coinciding again, he was rewarded with the post of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year, when the provincial examinations came round again, he was granted the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 歷蒙賜「壽」，頒賞御書及諸珍品，賜紫韁，紫禁城內坐二人暖輪，恩遇優渥。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he received the gift of the character "Longevity," was granted imperial calligraphy and various treasures, was given the purple bridle, and a two-seat heated carriage within the Forbidden City; his gracious treatment was exceptionally generous.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly honored with the character for longevity, imperial calligraphy, rare gifts, the purple bridle, and a heated two-seat carriage inside the Forbidden City—favors seldom bestowed so lavishly.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，再疏乞病，溫詔慰留。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he again memorialized begging leave for illness; a warm edict comforted him and urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 he again asked to retire on grounds of illness, but a gracious edict urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年八十有二，贈太傅，諡文正。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he died, aged eighty-two; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at eighty-two, and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 家鼐簡約斂退，生平無疾言遽色。

translations.literal: Jianai was simple and restrained in withdrawal; throughout his life he had no hasty words or sudden changes of countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Jianai lived plainly and quietly, and never spoke sharply or showed sudden anger.

sentences.zh: 雖貴，與諸生鈞禮。

translations.literal: Although eminent, he treated students with equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the height of his rank he treated students as equals.

sentences.zh: 閉門齋居，雜賓遠跡，推避權勢若怯。

translations.literal: He shut his door and dwelt in abstinence; miscellaneous guests kept their distance; he declined and avoided power as if timid.
translations.idiomatic: He kept to his study, turned casual visitors away, and shunned powerful patrons as though he were afraid of them.

sentences.zh: 嘗督湖北學政，典山西試，再典順天試，總裁會試，屢充閱卷大臣，獨無所私。

translations.literal: He once supervised Hubei education, presided over the Shanxi examination, twice presided over the Shuntian examination, served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination, and repeatedly served as examination-reading minister—alone showing no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: He had supervised education in Hubei, run the Shanxi and twice the Shuntian provincial exams, presided over the metropolitan examination, and served many times as chief reader—never once showing favoritism.

sentences.zh: 嘗拔一卷廁二甲，同列意不可，即屏退之，其讓不喜競類此。

translations.literal: Once he placed one examination booklet in the second class of the second rank; colleagues thought it unacceptable and he immediately set it aside; his yielding and dislike of competition were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Once he ranked a candidate in the second tier of the second class; when colleagues objected he withdrew the placement at once—he was always ready to yield and disliked contention.

sentences.zh: 器量尤廣，庚子，外人請懲禍首戮大臣，編修劉廷琛謂失國體，責宰輔不能爭，家鼐揖而引過。

translations.literal: His capacity was especially broad. In gengzi, foreigners asked to punish the ringleaders and execute great ministers; Compiler Liu Tingchen said this would lose national dignity and blamed the chief ministers for failing to remonstrate; Jianai bowed and took the blame upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was remarkably magnanimous. In 1900, when the powers demanded that ringleaders and senior ministers be punished, Compiler Liu Tingchen protested that this would humiliate the state and blamed the chief ministers for not resisting; Jianai bowed and accepted the reproach as his own fault.

sentences.zh: 其後詔舉御史。

translations.literal: Afterward an edict called for recommendations of censors.
translations.idiomatic: Later the throne ordered nominations for censorial posts.

sentences.zh: 家鼐獨保廷琛，謂曩以大義見責，知忠鯁必不負國，世皆稱之。

translations.literal: Jianai alone recommended Tingchen, saying that formerly, rebuked on great principle, he knew that the loyal and upright would surely not fail the state; the age all praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Jianai alone recommended Liu Tingchen, saying that a man who had once been rebuked for upholding the national interest would surely prove loyal; contemporaries praised the gesture widely.

sentences.zh: 張百熙，字埜秋，長沙人。

translations.literal: Zhang Baixi, style name Ye Qiu, was a man of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baixi, whose style was Ye Qiu, came from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi he became jinshi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Tongzhi 13 and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 督山東學政，典試四川。

translations.literal: He supervised Shandong education and presided over the Sichuan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised education in Shandong and ran the Sichuan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 命直南書房，再遷侍讀。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve in the Southern Study and was again promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Southern Study and was soon promoted again to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年，朝鮮釁起，朝議多主戰。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu trouble arose in Korea; court opinion mostly favored war.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 20, when conflict broke out in Korea, most at court favored war.

sentences.zh: 百熙疏劾李鴻章陽作戰備，陰實主和，左寶貴、聶士成皆勇敢善戰之將，以餉械不繼，遂致敗績，咎在鴻章；

translations.literal: Baixi memorialized impeaching Li Hongzhang for openly making war preparations while in secret actually favoring peace; Zuo Baogui and Nie Shicheng were both brave and skilled in battle, but because pay and weapons were not supplied in succession, defeat followed—the blame lay with Hongzhang;
translations.idiomatic: Baixi impeached Li Hongzhang for feigning war preparations while secretly favoring peace; he argued that generals Zuo Baogui and Nie Shicheng were brave and capable but had been defeated for lack of supplies, and that the fault lay with Li Hongzhang;

sentences.zh: 又劾禮親王世鐸筦樞務，招權納賄，戰事起，一倚鴻章，貽誤兵機：皆不報。

translations.literal: he also impeached Prince Li Shiduo for managing Grand Council affairs, monopolizing power and accepting bribes; when war arose he relied entirely on Hongzhang and thereby lost military opportunity—all went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: he also accused Prince Li Shiduo of monopolizing Grand Council power, taking bribes, and leaving military affairs entirely to Li Hongzhang—all to no response from the throne.

sentences.zh: 時值太后萬壽，承辦典禮者猶競尚華飾，百熙奏罷之。

translations.literal: It happened to be the Empress Dowager's birthday celebration; those in charge of the ceremonial still vied in extravagant display; Baixi memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When officials were still competing to lavish ornament on the Empress Dowager's birthday celebrations, Baixi persuaded the court to cancel them.

sentences.zh: 復偕侍講學士陸寶忠等合彈樞臣朋比誤國十大罪。

translations.literal: He again joined Expositor Lu Baozhong and others in jointly impeaching the Grand Council ministers for factional collusion harming the state in ten great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Expositor Lu Baozhong and others in charging the Grand Council with ten crimes of factional collusion that had harmed the state.

sentences.zh: 未幾，孫毓汶引疾歸，恭親王奕訢復入軍機，而百熙亦出督廣東學政。

translations.literal: Before long Sun Yuwen retired on grounds of illness; Prince Gong Yixin re-entered the Grand Council; and Baixi also went out to supervise Guangdong education.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sun Yuwen retired for illness, Prince Gong Yixin returned to the Grand Council, and Baixi was sent out to supervise education in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became a Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，坐濫舉康有爲，革職留任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, on the charge of indiscriminately recommending Kang Youwei, his office was removed but he was retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was stripped of rank but kept at his post for having indiscriminately recommended Kang Youwei.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授禮部侍郎，擢左都御史，充頭等專使大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, and made a first-rank special envoy minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he became Vice Minister of Rites, then Left Censor-in-Chief, and served as a first-rank special envoy.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂定，下詔求言，百熙抗疏陳大計，請改官制，理財政，變科舉，建學堂，設報館。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil was settled, an edict sought opinions; Baixi submitted a forthright memorial setting forth the great plan, asking to reform the official system, put finances in order, change the civil service examinations, build schools, and establish newspaper offices.
translations.idiomatic: After the Boxer uprising was suppressed, the throne called for memorials; Baixi laid out a sweeping program to reform the bureaucracy, overhaul finances, abolish the examinations, build schools, and found newspapers.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷工部尚書，調刑部，充管學大臣。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to Minister of Works, then shifted to the Ministry of Punishments, and served as Superintendent of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became Minister of Works, was transferred to Punishments, and was named Superintendent of Education.

sentences.zh: 京師之有大學堂也，始於中日戰後。

translations.literal: The capital's having a Imperial University began after the Sino-Japanese war.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing's Imperial University dated from the aftermath of the Sino-Japanese War.

sentences.zh: 侍郎李端棻奏請立學，中旨報可，而樞府厭言新政，請緩行。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Li Duanfen memorialized asking to establish the school; an imperial rescript approved, but the Grand Council disliked speaking of new policies and asked to defer implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Li Duanfen proposed founding the school and received imperial approval, but the Grand Council, hostile to reform, asked that it be postponed.

sentences.zh: 迄戊戌，乃奉嚴旨，促擬學章，命孫家鼐爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: By the wuxu year a stern edict was received urging drafting of school regulations; Sun Jianai was ordered to serve as Superintendent of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Not until 1898 did a stern edict order school regulations drafted at once and Sun Jianai named Superintendent of Education.

sentences.zh: 及政變，惟大學以萌芽早得不廢。

translations.literal: When the political coup came, only the university, because it had sprouted early, was not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After the coup of 1898 only the university survived, because it had been founded early enough to take root.

sentences.zh: 許景澄繼管學，坐論義和團被誅。

translations.literal: Xu Jingcheng succeeded in managing education; on the charge of discussing the Boxers he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingcheng succeeded him as superintendent but was executed for his views on the Boxers.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西幸，百熙詣行在，以人望被斯任，於是海內欣然望興學矣。

translations.literal: When the two palaces went west on campaign, Baixi went to the traveling court; because of public esteem he received this appointment; thereupon within the seas all gladly looked to the revival of learning.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled west, Baixi went to the traveling palace; his reputation won him the post, and the country looked to him to revive education with fresh hope.

sentences.zh: 百熙奏加冀州知州吳汝綸五品卿銜，總教大學。

translations.literal: Baixi memorialized to add to Jizhou Prefect Wu Rulun the fifth-rank honorary title of Qing, with overall charge of teaching at the university.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi asked that Jizhou prefect Wu Rulun be given fifth-rank honorary rank and placed in overall charge of instruction at the university.

sentences.zh: 汝綸辭不應，百熙具衣冠拜之，汝綸請赴日本察視學務。

translations.literal: Rulun declined and would not accept; Baixi put on full dress and cap and bowed to him; Rulun asked to go to Japan to inspect educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Rulun declined; Baixi dressed in full court robes and bowed to him in person; Rulun then asked leave to inspect schools in Japan.

sentences.zh: 大學教職員皆自聘，又薪金優厚，忌嫉者衆，蜚語浸聞。

translations.literal: The university's teaching and administrative staff were all personally engaged, and salaries were moreover generous; those who envied were many, and slander gradually reached the court.
translations.idiomatic: Because he hired the faculty himself and paid generous salaries, envy spread and rumors began to reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 汝綸返國，未至京，卒；

translations.literal: Rulun returned to the country but before reaching the capital died;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Rulun died on his way back to Beijing before he could arrive;

sentences.zh: 而百熙所倚以辦學者，門人沈兆祉亦受讒搆。

translations.literal: and Baixi's reliance for running the schools, his disciple Shen Zhaozhi, also suffered slander and framing.
translations.idiomatic: and Shen Zhaozhi, the disciple on whom Baixi had relied to run the schools, also fell victim to slander.

sentences.zh: 大學既負時謗，言官奏稱本朝定制，部官大率滿、漢相維，請更設滿大臣主教事，乃增命榮慶爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: The university having already borne contemporary slander, censorial officials memorialized saying that the present dynasty's established system was that ministry officials were mostly Manchu and Han in alternation; they asked to set up again a Manchu great minister to preside over affairs; thereupon Rongqing was additionally appointed Superintendent of Education.
translations.idiomatic: With the university under attack, censors argued that ministry posts should alternate between Manchu and Han officials and asked for a Manchu minister to share control; Rongqing was therefore added as co-superintendent.

sentences.zh: 旋別設學務處，以張亨嘉爲大學總監督，百熙權益分。

translations.literal: Shortly a separate Office of Educational Affairs was established; Zhang Hengjia was made overall supervisor of the university; Baixi's authority was further divided.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a separate Office of Educational Affairs was created, Zhang Hengjia was named overall university supervisor, and Baixi's authority was further reduced.

sentences.zh: 始議分建七科大學，又選派諸生游學東西洋。

translations.literal: At first it was proposed to build separately seven specialized universities; students were also selected and sent to study in the East and West.
translations.idiomatic: He first proposed seven specialized universities and began selecting students to study abroad in Europe and Japan.

sentences.zh: 榮慶意不謂可，而百熙持之堅，親至站送諸生登車。

translations.literal: Rongqing's opinion was that it was not advisable, but Baixi held to it firmly and personally went to the station to see the students board the train.
translations.idiomatic: Rongqing disapproved, but Baixi held firm and went in person to the station to see the students off.

sentences.zh: 各省之派官費生自此始。

translations.literal: The provinces' dispatch of government-funded students began from this.
translations.idiomatic: This marked the beginning of provincial government-funded study abroad.

sentences.zh: 值張之洞入覲，命改定學章，及還鎮，復命家鼐爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Zhidong came to audience; he was ordered to revise the school regulations; when he returned to his post, Jianai was again ordered as Superintendent of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhidong came to court he was told to revise the regulations; after he returned to his post Sun Jianai was again named superintendent.

sentences.zh: 凡三管學，百熙位第三矣。

translations.literal: In all there were three superintendents of education; Baixi stood third.
translations.idiomatic: There had been three superintendents in all, and Baixi was the third.

sentences.zh: 百熙擬建分科大學，以絀於貲而止，惟創醫學及譯學館、實業館，遽謝學務。

translations.literal: Baixi planned to build specialized branch universities; because funds were short he stopped; he only founded medical, translation, and industrial schools, then quickly resigned educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi planned specialized universities but stopped for lack of funds; he founded only medical, translation, and industrial schools, then soon left educational affairs.

sentences.zh: 賞黃馬褂、紫禁城騎馬。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with the yellow jacket and permission to ride a horse within the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the yellow jacket and the privilege of riding inside the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 後歷禮部、戶部、郵傳部尚書，政務、學務、編纂官制諸大臣。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Minister of Rites, Revenue, and Posts and Communications, and as minister of government affairs, education, and compilation of the official system.
translations.idiomatic: He later headed the Ministries of Rites, Revenue, and Posts and Communications, and served on the boards for government affairs, education, and bureaucratic reform.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保，諡文達。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wenda.

sentences.zh: 唐景崇，字春卿，廣西灌陽人。

translations.literal: Tang Jingchong, style name Chunqing, was a man of Guanyang, Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jingchong, whose style was Chunqing, came from Guanyang in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 父懋功，舉人，有學行。

translations.literal: His father Maogong was a provincial graduate and possessed learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maogong was a provincial graduate known for scholarship and integrity.

sentences.zh: 景崇，同治十年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: Jingchong, in the tenth year of Tongzhi became jinshi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong passed the jinshi examination in Tongzhi 10 and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 由侍讀四遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: From Reader-in-Waiting he was promoted four times to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Reader-in-Waiting through four promotions to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年，典試廣東。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he presided over the Guangdong examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 20 he ran the Guangdong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年，主會試。

translations.literal: The following year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he presided over the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部、禮部侍郎，權左都御史，出督浙江學政，母憂歸。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Minister of War and Rites, acting Left Censor-in-Chief, went out to supervise Zhejiang education, and returned on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of War and Rites, acting Left Censor-in-Chief, then supervised education in Zhejiang until he returned home for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 拳禍起，命督辦廣西團練。

translations.literal: When the Boxer calamity arose he was ordered to supervise Guangxi militia training.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer crisis broke out he was ordered to organize militia in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以工部侍郎典試浙江，督江蘇學政，三十一年，詔罷科歲試，學政專司考校學務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, as Vice Minister of Works he presided over the Zhejiang examination and supervised Jiangsu education; in the thirty-first year an edict abolished the annual civil examination cycle; education commissioners were solely charged with examining and supervising educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, as Vice Minister of Works, he ran the Zhejiang examination and supervised Jiangsu schools; in the thirty-first year the throne abolished annual provincial examinations and made education commissioners responsible only for school oversight.

sentences.zh: 景崇條上十事。

translations.literal: Jingchong itemized and submitted ten matters.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong submitted a ten-point program.

sentences.zh: 明年，罷學政，還京供職。

translations.literal: The following year he was removed as education commissioner and returned to the capital to take up duty.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he left the education commission and returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 疏陳立憲大要四事。

translations.literal: He memorialized setting forth four main points of constitutional government.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on four essentials of constitutional government.

sentences.zh: 時兩廣疆臣建議廣西省會移治南寧，京朝官皆持異議。

translations.literal: At that time the frontier officials of the two Guang provinces proposed moving the Guangxi provincial capital to Nanning; capital officials all held differing opinions.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier officials in Guangdong and Guangxi proposed moving the Guangxi capital from Guilin to Nanning, most officials in Beijing objected.

sentences.zh: 景崇奏陳：「遷省之議，以越南逼近龍州，法人時蓄狡謀，桂林距離遠，聲氣難通，不若改建南寧之便。

translations.literal: Jingchong memorialized, stating: "The proposal to move the provincial seat holds that because Vietnam presses close to Longzhou and the French at times harbor crafty designs, Guilin is far in distance and voice and breath are hard to connect—better to rebuild at Nanning."
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong replied: "Advocates of the move argue that with Vietnam pressing on Longzhou and French designs never far away, Guilin is too remote to command the frontier, and Nanning would be more convenient."

sentences.zh: 臣謂不然，今我兵力尚不能經營邕州，扼北海水陸衝要，徒虛張聲勢，招外人疑忌何爲？

translations.literal: Your servant says this is not so: now our military strength still cannot manage Yongzhou and hold the land and water strategic points of Beihai—only vainly expanding prestige and inviting foreigners' suspicion and jealousy—for what purpose?
translations.idiomatic: "I disagree. We cannot yet even hold Yongzhou and the Beihai land and sea approaches in force; what good is it to make an empty show of power and invite foreign suspicion?"

sentences.zh: 且遷徙締造之費，桂林善後之費，練兵設防之費，皆非巨款不辦。

translations.literal: Moreover the costs of migration and construction, the costs of Guilin's aftermath, the costs of drilling troops and setting defenses—all cannot be managed without huge funds.
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover the costs of building a new capital, maintaining Guilin, and raising troops for defense cannot be met without enormous sums."

sentences.zh: 方今俄居西陲，英窺南徼，蒙、藏、川、滇勢均岌岌，非獨一法人之可畏。

translations.literal: Just now Russia occupies the western marches, England peers at the southern frontiers; Mongolia, Tibet, Sichuan, and Yunnan are all in peril alike—it is not only the French who are to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: "Russia presses the northwest, Britain watches the south, and Mongolia, Tibet, Sichuan, and Yunnan are all precarious; France is not our only concern."

sentences.zh: 以大局論，決不能竭全力事廣西之一隅；

translations.literal: Speaking from the larger pattern, one absolutely cannot exhaust full strength on one corner of Guangxi;
translations.idiomatic: "From the standpoint of the empire, the court cannot pour all its strength into one corner of Guangxi;"

sentences.zh: 以廣西論，亦不能竭全力事南寧之一隅：明矣。

translations.literal: speaking from Guangxi, one also cannot exhaust full strength on one corner at Nanning—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: "and Guangxi itself cannot pour all its resources into Nanning alone. That much is clear."

sentences.zh: 故爲今之計，誠能簡重臣駐龍州，於對汛邊地二千里，相度土宜，興辦樹藝、屯墾、畜牧、開礦諸端，俟地利漸興，人齒漸繁，再以兵法部勒。

translations.literal: Therefore for the present plan, if one can truly select a weighty minister to reside at Longzhou, along the two thousand li of border facing the enemy posts, survey soil suitability, and undertake tree planting, reclamation colonies, animal husbandry, and mining and other items, wait until geographical advantage gradually rises and population gradually grows dense, then again apply military law to organize—
translations.idiomatic: "The better course is to station a senior official at Longzhou, develop the two-thousand-li border through forestry, reclamation, livestock, and mining, and only after the land grows prosperous and the population denser apply military organization."

sentences.zh: 此上策也。

translations.literal: this is the superior strategy.
translations.idiomatic: "That is the best long-term policy."

sentences.zh: 至目前應變之方，莫如迅設龍州電綫，移提督駐南寧，增募十營，暫停廣西應解賠款，飭各省欠解廣西協餉，分年攤解，用抵賠款。

translations.literal: As to the present method of meeting change, nothing is better than swiftly establishing a Longzhou telegraph line, moving the provincial military commander to reside at Nanning, increasing recruitment by ten battalions, temporarily suspending Guangxi's payable indemnity installments, and ordering the provinces' arrears in Guangxi cooperative pay to be paid in installments by year, using them to offset indemnity payments.
translations.idiomatic: "For immediate needs, the court should run a telegraph line to Longzhou, move the provincial commander to Nanning, raise ten new battalions, suspend Guangxi's indemnity payments for the time being, and have other provinces pay their overdue cooperative subsidies to Guangxi in yearly installments to offset indemnity obligations."

sentences.zh: 一轉移間，餉足則兵强，可紓朝廷南顧之憂。

translations.literal: With one shift, if pay is sufficient then troops are strong, and the court's anxiety in looking south can be eased.
translations.idiomatic: "Once funds and troops are in place, the court's anxieties about the south can be eased."

sentences.zh: 若遷省之舉，勞民費財，無益於治。

translations.literal: If it is the act of moving the provincial seat, it toils the people and spends wealth, with no benefit to governance.
translations.idiomatic: "Moving the capital would burden the people, waste money, and do nothing for good government."

sentences.zh: 」事得寢。

translations.literal: " The matter thereby came to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 調吏部侍郎，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 景崇以績學端品受主知，屢司文柄。

translations.literal: Jingchong, through solid learning and upright character, received the ruler's trust and repeatedly held the literary brush of office.
translations.idiomatic: Known for solid scholarship and upright character, he won the emperor's trust and repeatedly controlled the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 迨科舉罷，廷試游學畢業生，皆倚景崇校閱。

translations.literal: When the civil service examinations were abolished, the palace examination of students graduating from study abroad all relied on Jingchong for examination and review.
translations.idiomatic: After the examinations were abolished, the palace tests for students returning from study abroad were entrusted to his review.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，戴鴻慈卒，遺疏薦景崇堪大用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong Dai Hongci died; in his final memorial he recommended Jingchong as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 Dai Hongci died and in his final memorial recommended Jingchong as a man of outstanding ability.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢學部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔設內閣，改學務大臣。

translations.literal: The following year an edict established the cabinet; he was changed to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the cabinet was created, he was renamed Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 是時學說紛歧，景崇力謀溝通新舊，慎擇教科書。

translations.literal: At that time doctrines were divided and conflicting; Jingchong strove to bridge old and new and carefully chose textbooks.
translations.idiomatic: At a time of fierce doctrinal dispute, he worked to reconcile old and new learning and chose textbooks with care.

sentences.zh: 兼任弼德院顧問大臣。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as advisory minister of the Hall for Nurturing Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as an adviser to the Hall for Nurturing Virtue.

sentences.zh: 武昌變起，袁世凱總理內閣，仍命掌學務。

translations.literal: When the Wuchang uprising arose, Yuan Shikai headed the cabinet and still ordered him to manage educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wuchang uprising Yuan Shikai formed a cabinet and still left him in charge of education.

sentences.zh: 引疾去。

translations.literal: He cited illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 越三年，卒，諡文簡。

translations.literal: After three years he died and was given the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died and received the posthumous title Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 景崇博覽羣書，通天文算術，尤喜治史。

translations.literal: Jingchong broadly read the classics, mastered astronomy and mathematics, and especially delighted in studying history.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong read widely, mastered astronomy and mathematics, and above all loved historical study.

sentences.zh: 自爲編修時，取新唐書爲作注，大例有三：曰糾繆，曰補闕，曰疏解，甄采書逾數百種。

translations.literal: From the time he was a Compiler he took the New Book of Tang to write commentary; the great categories were three: called Correcting Errors, called Supplementing Omissions, and called Explicating and Resolving; he selected and gathered from books exceeding several hundred kinds.
translations.idiomatic: As a Compiler he began annotating the New Book of Tang under three headings—Correcting Errors, Supplementing Omissions, and Explication—drawing on more than four hundred works.

sentences.zh: 家故貧，得秘籍精本，輒典質購之。

translations.literal: His family was originally poor; whenever he obtained rare books and fine editions he would pawn items to purchase them.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and whenever he found a rare edition he would pawn belongings to buy it.

sentences.zh: 殫精畢世，唯缺地理志內羈縻州及藝文志，餘均脫稿。

translations.literal: He exhausted his spirit through his lifetime; only the geographical treatise's inner dependent prefectures and the bibliography were lacking; the rest were all in finished draft.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted his life to the project; only the sections on dependent prefectures in the geography monograph and the bibliography remained unfinished, and the rest was complete in draft.

sentences.zh: 于式枚，字晦若，賀縣人。

translations.literal: Yu Shimei, style name Huiruo, was a man of Hexian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shimei, whose style was Huiruo, came from Hexian.

sentences.zh: 博聞强記，善屬文。

translations.literal: Broadly informed with a powerful memory, he was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He had a prodigious memory and wrote with ease.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年進士，以庶吉士，散館用兵部主事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he became jinshi; as a Hanlin bachelor, on leaving the academy he was assigned as a principal clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Guangxu 6, served as a Hanlin bachelor, and on leaving the academy was assigned to the Ministry of War as a principal clerk.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏調北洋差遣，歷十餘年，奏牘多出其手。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized to transfer him to Beiyang service; over more than ten years most memorials and documents came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang had him transferred to Beiyang service, and for more than ten years most of Li's memorials were drafted by him.

sentences.zh: 性不樂爲外吏，又格於例不得保升京秩，久之不遷。

translations.literal: By nature he did not delight in serving as an outside official; moreover, blocked by precedent he could not be recommended for promotion to capital rank; for a long time he was not transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked service outside the capital, and precedent barred him from promotion to Beijing rank, so for years he received no advancement.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，鴻章賀俄皇加冕，因歷聘德、法、英、美諸國，式枚充隨員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Hongzhang attended the Russian emperor's coronation and thereby made successive embassies to Germany, France, England, America, and other states; Shimei served as an attendant member.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Li Hongzhang attended the Russian coronation and toured Germany, France, Britain, and the United States, with Shimei on his staff.

sentences.zh: 俄選授禮部主事，由員外郎授御史，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Shortly he was selected and appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites; from department vice director he was appointed censor and promoted to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to the Ministry of Rites, rose from vice director to censor, and was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 贊辛丑和約，賞五品京堂。

translations.literal: For assisting the xinchou peace treaty he was rewarded with fifth-rank capital bureau rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in the 1901 peace settlement he was granted fifth-rank capital bureau rank.

sentences.zh: 充政務處幫提調、大學堂總辦、譯學館監督。

translations.literal: He served as assistant coordinator of the Office of Government Affairs, overall manager of the Imperial University, and supervisor of the School of Translation.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant coordinator of the Government Affairs Office, overall manager of the Imperial University, and supervisor of the School of Translation.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，以鴻臚寺少卿督廣東學政，改提學使，疏辭，命總理廣西鐵路。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments he supervised Guangdong education; he was changed to education commissioner, memorialized to decline, and was ordered to take overall charge of the Guangxi railway.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was sent to supervise Guangdong education as vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, declined the post of education commissioner when it was offered, and was ordered to oversee the Guangxi railway.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，擢郵傳部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Posts and Communications.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Posts and Communications.

sentences.zh: 當是時，政潮激烈，有詔預備立憲，舉朝競言西法，無敢持異議者。

translations.literal: At that time political currents were fierce; an edict announced preparation for constitutional government; the whole court vied in speaking of Western methods, and none dared hold differing opinions.
translations.idiomatic: Political passions ran high; the throne had announced constitutional preparation, and the whole court rushed to praise Western models with scarcely a dissenting voice.

sentences.zh: 於是式枚奉命出使德國，充考察憲政大臣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shimei received orders to go on embassy to Germany as minister investigating constitutional government.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei was then ordered to Germany as minister charged with studying constitutional government.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，疏言：「憲政必以本國爲根據，采取他國以輔益之，在求其實，不徒震其名。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he memorialized, saying: "Constitutional government must take one's own country as foundation, adopt other countries to supplement and enrich it; the aim lies in seeking the substance, not merely being awed by the name."
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he wrote: "Constitutional government must be rooted in our own country and draw on foreign models only to supplement it; we must seek substance, not be dazzled by names."

sentences.zh: 我朝道監百王，科條詳備，行政皆守部章，風聞亦許言事，刑賞予奪，曾不自私。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's Way oversees the hundred kings; statutes and regulations are detailed and complete; administration all follows ministry regulations; hearsay is also permitted to report affairs; punishments, rewards, grants, and withdrawals have never been selfish.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's institutions already encompass the wisdom of ages: regulations are detailed, ministries govern by rule, rumor may be reported upward, and rewards and punishments have never been arbitrary.

sentences.zh: 有大政事、大興革，內則集廷臣之議，外或待疆吏之章。

translations.literal: When there were great state affairs or great innovations, within the court ministers' deliberations were gathered; outside one sometimes awaited frontier officials' memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Major policies and reforms are debated within the court and often await memorials from provincial officials.

sentences.zh: 勤求民隱，博采公論，與立憲之制無不符合。

translations.literal: Diligently seeking the people's hidden grievances and broadly gathering public opinion accord in nothing with the constitutional system.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent inquiry into popular grievances and broad consultation match constitutional practice in every respect.

sentences.zh: 上有教誡無約誓，下有遵守無要求。

translations.literal: Above there is instruction and admonition without covenant oaths; below there is observance without demands.
translations.idiomatic: The throne instructs without binding oaths, and subjects obey without making demands.

sentences.zh: 至日久官吏失職，或有奉行之不善，海國開通，又有事例之所無，自可因時損益，並非變法更張。

translations.literal: As to the passage of years when officials lost their duties, or there was unskillful execution, and maritime countries opened relations, there were also matters without precedent—one may naturally adjust according to the times; this is not changing the law and overturning institutions.
translations.idiomatic: When officials fail in their duties, policies are poorly executed, or new maritime contacts raise unprecedented cases, adjustments may be made in due course without overturning the fundamental system.

sentences.zh: 惟人心趣向各異，告以堯、舜、周、孔之道，則以爲不足法；

translations.literal: Only people's minds and inclinations differ; told of the Way of Yao, Shun, Zhou, and Confucius, they consider it insufficient as model;
translations.idiomatic: Minds differ widely: told of Yao, Shun, the Zhou, and Confucius, many deem them inadequate models;

sentences.zh: 告以英、德、法、美之制度，而日本所模仿者，則心悅誠服，以爲當行。

translations.literal: told of the systems of England, Germany, France, and America—and what Japan imitated—they are pleased in heart and sincere in submission, holding that these ought to be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: but shown the institutions of Britain, Germany, France, America, and Japan's adaptations of them, they embrace them wholeheartedly as what must be done.

sentences.zh: 考日本維新之初，即宣言立憲之意。

translations.literal: Examining Japan at the beginning of its restoration, it immediately proclaimed the intent of constitutional government.
translations.idiomatic: Japan proclaimed constitutional intentions at the very start of the Meiji Restoration.

sentences.zh: 後十四年，始發布開設國會之敕諭，二十年乃頒行憲法。

translations.literal: Fourteen years later it first issued the edict announcing the opening of a national assembly; only in the twentieth year did it promulgate the constitution.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen years passed before it ordered a parliament convened, and twenty before the constitution was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 蓋預備詳密遲慎如此。

translations.literal: Thus its preparation was detailed, slow, and cautious to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Its preparation was as deliberate and cautious as that.

sentences.zh: 今橫議者自謂國民，聚衆者輒云團體，數年之中，內治外交，用人行政，皆有干預之想。

translations.literal: Now those who speak rashly call themselves nationals; those who gather crowds readily say "organization"; within a few years, in internal governance and foreign relations, appointment of personnel and administration—all have thoughts of intervention.
translations.idiomatic: Today rash critics call themselves "the people," agitators form "organizations," and within a few years they seek to intervene in domestic policy, foreign affairs, appointments, and administration alike.

sentences.zh: 動以立憲爲詞，紛馳電函，上厪宸慮。

translations.literal: They constantly take constitutional government as their slogan, sending telegrams and letters in confusion, troubling the imperial mind above.
translations.idiomatic: They invoke constitutionalism at every turn, bombard the throne with telegrams, and trouble the emperor's peace of mind.

sentences.zh: 蓋以立憲爲新奇可喜，不知吾國所自有。

translations.literal: They take constitutional government as novel and pleasing, not knowing what our country already possesses of its own.
translations.idiomatic: They treat constitutionalism as a novelty, unaware that China already possesses its essentials.

sentences.zh: 其關於學術者，固貽譏荒陋，以立憲爲即可施行，不審東洋之近事。

translations.literal: As to what concerns learning, they indeed invite ridicule for crudeness; holding constitutional government as immediately implementable, they do not examine recent events in the Eastern Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship they invite ridicule for crudeness; in politics they assume a constitution can be imposed overnight without studying Japan's recent experience.

sentences.zh: 關於政術者，尤有害治安。

translations.literal: As to what concerns political method, it is especially harmful to public order.
translations.idiomatic: Their political demands are especially dangerous to public order.

sentences.zh: 惟在朝廷本一定之指歸，齊萬衆之心志，循序漸進。

translations.literal: It lies only in the court's holding to a fixed direction, aligning the myriad people's minds and wills, and advancing step by step in order.
translations.idiomatic: The court must hold a clear course, align public opinion, and advance step by step.

sentences.zh: 先設京師議院以定從違，舉辦地方自治以植根本，尤要在廣興教育，儲備人才。

translations.literal: First establish a capital assembly to determine assent and dissent; undertake local self-government to plant roots; above all it lies in broadly promoting education and storing up talent.
translations.idiomatic: It should first establish a capital assembly, promote local self-government, and above all expand education and train talent.

sentences.zh: 凡與憲政相輔而行者，均當先事綢繆者也。

translations.literal: All matters that assist constitutional government in parallel operation should likewise be prepared beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Every measure that supports constitutional government must be prepared in advance.

sentences.zh: 臣前隨李鴻章至柏林，略觀大概。

translations.literal: Your servant formerly followed Li Hongzhang to Berlin and briefly observed the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: I once accompanied Li Hongzhang to Berlin and gained some general impressions.

sentences.zh: 今承特簡，謹當參合中、西同異，歸極於皇朝典章，庶言皆有本而事屬可行。

translations.literal: Now receiving special selection, I shall respectfully combine Chinese and Western similarities and differences and return to the ultimate in the imperial dynasty's statutes, so that words may all have foundation and affairs belong to what can be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Now specially commissioned, I shall compare Chinese and Western institutions and ground my report in the dynasty's own statutes, so that every proposal has a basis and can be carried out.

sentences.zh: 是臣區區之至願。

translations.literal: This is your servant's humble utmost wish.
translations.idiomatic: That is my humble earnest wish.

sentences.zh: 明年，調禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時新黨要求實行立憲，召集國會日亟。

translations.literal: At that time the New Party demanded implementation of constitutional government; the day for convening a national assembly grew urgent daily.
translations.idiomatic: Reformers were pressing for immediate constitutional government and demanding that a parliament be convened without delay.

sentences.zh: 式枚上言：「臣徧考東西歷史，參校同異，大抵中法皆定自上而下奉行，西法則定自下而上遵守。

translations.literal: Shimei submitted, saying: "Your servant has broadly examined Eastern and Western history and compared similarities and differences; in general Chinese methods are all fixed from above downward for implementation, while Western methods are fixed from below upward for observance."
translations.idiomatic: Shimei wrote: "Having surveyed Eastern and Western history, I find that in China institutions are ordained from above and obeyed downward, whereas in the West they arise from below and are upheld upward."

sentences.zh: 惟日本憲法，則纂自日臣伊藤博文，雖西國之名詞，仍東洋之性質。

translations.literal: Only Japan's constitution was compiled by the Japanese minister Ito Hirobumi; although using Western countries' terminology, it still bears the Eastern Ocean's character.
translations.idiomatic: Japan's constitution was drafted by Ito Hirobumi: though couched in Western terms, it remains essentially East Asian in character.

sentences.zh: 其采取則普魯士爲多，其本原則德君臣所定，名爲欽定憲法。

translations.literal: In what it adopted Prussia predominated; in its origin it was fixed by German ruler and ministers, called an imperially granted constitution.
translations.idiomatic: It drew chiefly on Prussia and was promulgated by the German emperor and his ministers as an imperially granted constitution.

sentences.zh: 夫國所以立曰政，政所以行曰權，權所歸即利所在。

translations.literal: What establishes a state is called government; what executes government is called power; where power returns is where benefit lies.
translations.idiomatic: A state rests on government, government rests on power, and power is where interest lies.

sentences.zh: 定於一則無非分之想，散於衆則有競進之心。

translations.literal: Fixed in one there are no improper thoughts; scattered among the multitude there is a mind to compete and advance.
translations.idiomatic: When power is unified, improper ambitions fade; when it is dispersed, rivalry and ambition flourish.

sentences.zh: 行之而善，則爲日本之維新；

translations.literal: If implemented well, it becomes Japan's restoration;
translations.idiomatic: Well managed, it produces Japan's restoration;

sentences.zh: 行之不善，則爲法國之革命。

translations.literal: if implemented poorly, it becomes France's revolution.
translations.idiomatic: poorly managed, France's revolution.

sentences.zh: 法國當屢世苛虐之後，民困已深，欲以立憲救亡，而適促其亂。

translations.literal: France, after generations of harsh cruelty, had the people's hardship already deep; wishing to save the state through constitutional government, it instead hastened its disorder.
translations.idiomatic: France, after generations of oppression, was so deeply exhausted that constitutionalism meant to save the state only hastened disorder.

sentences.zh: 日本當尊王傾幕之時，本由民力，故以立憲爲報，而猶緩其期。

translations.literal: Japan, at the time of honoring the ruler and overthrowing the shogunate, was fundamentally by the people's strength; therefore it took constitutional government as repayment, yet still slowed the term.
translations.idiomatic: Japan's restoration rested on popular support, so it rewarded the people with constitutional promises yet still moved slowly.

sentences.zh: 中國名義最重，政治最寬，國體尊嚴，人情安習，既無法國之怨毒，又非日本之改造。

translations.literal: China's nominal propriety is weightiest, its politics most lenient; national dignity is august; popular sentiment is settled in habit; it has neither France's resentful poison nor Japan's transformation.
translations.idiomatic: China values ritual propriety above all, governs leniently, and enjoys settled customs; it lacks France's accumulated bitterness and is not undergoing Japan's wholesale transformation.

sentences.zh: 皇上俯順輿情，迭降諭旨，分定年期，自宜互相奮勉，靜待推行。

translations.literal: The Emperor, bending to follow public sentiment, repeatedly issued edicts, apportioning fixed years; all should mutually encourage one another and quietly await implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor has already heeded public opinion, issued repeated edicts, and set a timetable; all should work diligently and wait calmly for gradual implementation.

sentences.zh: 豈容欲速等於取償，求治同於論價？

translations.literal: How can one allow haste to equal demanding repayment, or seeking order to equal haggling over price?
translations.idiomatic: How can reform be rushed like collecting a debt, or good government bargained for like goods in a market?

sentences.zh: 至敢言監督朝廷，推倒政府，胥動浮言，幾同亂黨。

translations.literal: As for daring to speak of supervising the court, overthrowing the government—all move with empty words, nearly the same as disorderly factions.
translations.idiomatic: Those who dare speak of supervising the throne and overthrowing the government trade in empty slogans and are scarcely distinguishable from rebels.

sentences.zh: 欲圖補救之策，惟在朝廷舉錯一秉至公，不稍予以指摘之端，自無從爲煽惑之計。

translations.literal: If one wishes to plan remedial measures, it lies only in the court's actions and errors all holding to utmost fairness, not slightly giving grounds for criticism—then naturally there is no means for schemes of incitement.
translations.idiomatic: The remedy lies in the court's conducting itself with perfect fairness and giving agitators no handle for complaint.

sentences.zh: 至東南各省疆吏，當慎擇有風力、知大體者鎮懾之。

translations.literal: As for the southeastern provinces' frontier officials, one should carefully choose those with force of character who understand the larger pattern to suppress and awe them.
translations.idiomatic: In the southeast, frontier officials of force and judgment should be chosen to keep order.

sentences.zh: 當十年預備之期，爲大局安危所繫。

translations.literal: The ten-year preparatory period bears on the larger pattern's safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: The ten-year preparatory period is vital to the nation's safety.

sentences.zh: 日皇所謂『組織權限，爲朕親裁』，德相所謂『法定於君，非民可解』。

translations.literal: What the Japanese emperor called "organizing authority, personally decided by Us," what the German chancellor called "law fixed by the ruler, not to be interpreted by the people."
translations.idiomatic: As the Japanese emperor said, "organizing authority is for Us personally to decide," and the German chancellor said, "law is fixed by the ruler and not subject to popular interpretation."

sentences.zh: 故必正名定分，然後措正施行。

translations.literal: Therefore one must rectify names and fix roles, and only then arrange and implement correctly.
translations.idiomatic: Names and roles must be clarified before institutions can be put into proper practice.

sentences.zh: 臣濫膺考察，斷不敢附會時趨，貽誤國家，得罪名教。

translations.literal: Your servant undeservedly received the investigation commission; I absolutely dare not echo the times' trend, bring error to the state, or offend the teachings of names.
translations.idiomatic: Though unworthy of this commission, I dare not trim my views to fashion, harm the state, or betray the moral order.

sentences.zh: 」章下所司。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 上海政聞社法部主事陳景仁等電請定三年內開國會，罷式枚謝天下，嚴旨申飭，褫景仁職。

translations.literal: Chen Jingren of the Shanghai Political News Society, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, and others telegraphed asking to fix opening a national assembly within three years and dismiss Shimei to apologize to the realm; a stern edict rebuked them and stripped Jingren of office.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingren of Shanghai's Political News Society telegraphed demanding a parliament within three years and Shimei's dismissal; the throne rebuked them sharply and stripped Chen of office.

sentences.zh: 式枚復奏言：「德皇接受國書，答言憲政紛繁，慮未必合中國用，選舉法尤未易行。

translations.literal: Shimei again memorialized, saying: "The German emperor, receiving the credentials, replied that constitutional government is complex and tangled, and he feared it might not suit China's use; election law especially is not easy to implement."
translations.idiomatic: Shimei reported that the German emperor, receiving China's credentials, said constitutional government was complex and might not suit China, and that election laws would be especially hard to apply.

sentences.zh: 又昔英儒斯賓塞爾亦甚言憲法流弊，謂美國憲法本人民平等，行之久而治權握於政黨，平民不勝其苦。

translations.literal: Moreover the former English scholar Spencer also spoke at length of constitutional government's abuses, saying America's constitution was originally based on popular equality, but after long implementation governing power was held by political parties and common people could not bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: The English thinker Spencer likewise warned of constitutional abuses, noting that though the American constitution began in popular equality, power soon passed to parties and the common people suffered under them.

sentences.zh: 蓋歐人言憲法，其難其慎如此。

translations.literal: Thus when Europeans speak of constitutional government, its difficulty and caution are to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Europeans themselves treat constitutional government with such difficulty and caution.

sentences.zh: 今橫議遍於國中，上則詆政府固權，下則罵國民失職，專以爭競相勸導。

translations.literal: Now rash opinion spreads throughout the country; above they slander the government for monopolizing power; below they revile nationals for failing their duties; they specialize in encouraging rivalry and competition.
translations.idiomatic: Today reckless talk fills the land: critics above denounce the government for clinging to power, critics below blame the people for failing their duties, and all preach contention.

sentences.zh: 此正斯賓塞爾所云政黨者流，與平民固無與也。

translations.literal: These are precisely what Spencer called the party faction—having in fact nothing to do with common people.
translations.idiomatic: These are precisely the party factions Spencer described, with nothing to do with the common people.

sentences.zh: 伊藤博文論君臣相與，先道德而後科條。

translations.literal: Ito Hirobumi discussed ruler and minister interacting: first morality, afterward statutes and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ito Hirobumi held that relations between ruler and minister require morality before statutes.

sentences.zh: 君民何獨不然？

translations.literal: Why should ruler and people alone not be so?
translations.idiomatic: Why should relations between ruler and people be any different?

sentences.zh: 果能誠信相接，則普與日本以欽定憲法行之至今；

translations.literal: If one can truly connect in sincerity and trust, then Prussia and Japan, with imperially granted constitutions, have implemented them to the present;
translations.idiomatic: If sincerity and trust prevail, Prussia and Japan have governed successfully under imperially granted constitutions to this day;

sentences.zh: 如其不然，則法蘭西固民約憲法，何以革命者再三，改法者數十而猶未定？

translations.literal: if not so, then France indeed has a popular covenant constitution—why have revolutions come again and again, and legal changes dozens of times, yet still not be settled?
translations.idiomatic: if not, why has France, for all its popular constitution, suffered repeated revolutions and dozens of constitutional revisions without ever settling?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲中國立憲，應以日本仿照普魯士之例爲權衡，以畢士麥由君主用人民意見制定，及伊藤博文先道德後科條之言爲標準，則憲法大綱立矣。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly holds that China's establishing constitutional government should take Japan's imitation of the Prussian example as measure, and take Bismarck's words on the ruler using the people's opinions to formulate, and Ito Hirobumi's words on morality before statutes, as standard—then the constitutional outline would be established.
translations.idiomatic: I believe China should follow Japan's Prussian model, Bismarck's principle that the monarch shapes law with popular input, and Ito's insistence on morality before statutes; then the constitutional framework would be sound.

sentences.zh: 」章下所司。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 又以各省諮議局章程與普國地方議會制度不符，大恉謂：「改革未定之時，中央政權唯恐少統一堅强之力，而國民識政體知法意者極少。

translations.literal: He also held that the provincial deliberative assembly regulations did not accord with Prussia's local parliament system, and stated in great outline: "While reform is not yet settled, central governing power fears only lacking unified, strong force, while nationals who understand political systems and know legal intent are extremely few."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that provincial deliberative assembly regulations diverged from Prussian local parliaments and wrote: "While reform remains unsettled, central authority can scarcely afford to weaken unified control, and few citizens understand government or law."

sentences.zh: 驟以此龐大政權之地方議會，橫亙政府與國民之間，縱使被選者不皆營私武斷，而一國政權落於最少數人之手，劫持中外大臣，後患何可勝言？

translations.literal: Suddenly placing this enormous governing power in local parliaments, stretching across between government and nationals—even if those elected are not all pursuing private gain and arbitrary rule—yet a state's governing power falls into the hands of the smallest minority, coercing Chinese and foreign great ministers; later troubles—how can they all be told?
translations.idiomatic: To thrust such vast authority into local assemblies between throne and people—even if the elected were not all corrupt—would concentrate national power in a tiny minority able to coerce ministers at home and abroad, with consequences beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 」因證以普制，逐條駁議。

translations.literal: " Thereupon citing Prussian institutions, he rebutted article by article.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Prussian institutions and rebutted the regulations clause by clause.

sentences.zh: 先後譯奏普魯士憲法全文、官制位號等級，暨兩議院新舊選舉法。

translations.literal: Successively he translated and memorialized the full text of the Prussian constitution, official system ranks and grades, and the two chambers' old and new election laws.
translations.idiomatic: He translated and submitted the full Prussian constitution, the official rank system, and the old and new election laws of both chambers.

sentences.zh: 式枚以三十三年冬行，宣統元年六月返國，以疾乞假。

translations.literal: Shimei departed in the winter of the thirty-third year; in the sixth month of the first year of Xuantong he returned to the country and begged leave for illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei left in the winter of the thirty-third year and returned in the sixth month of Xuantong 1, then asked sick leave.

sentences.zh: 張之洞遺疏薦式枚堪大用。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong's final memorial recommended Shimei as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong's final memorial recommended Shimei as a man of outstanding ability.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部侍郎，改學部侍郎，總理禮學館事、修訂法律大臣、國史館副總裁。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, changed to Vice Minister of Education, took overall charge of the Hall of Ritual Learning, served as minister for revising the laws, and was vice president of the National History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister of Personnel, then Education, oversaw the Hall of Ritual Learning, served as minister for legal revision, and was vice president of the National History Office.

sentences.zh: 國變後，僑居青島。

translations.literal: After the change of dynasty he lived abroad in Qingdao.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he lived in exile in Qingdao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年六十三，諡文和。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-three, and was given the posthumous title Wenhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at sixty-three, with the posthumous title Wenhe.

sentences.zh: 式枚生而隱宮，精力絕人，夜倚枕坐如枯僧。

translations.literal: Shimei was born with a hidden palace defect; his energy surpassed others; at night he leaned on a pillow and sat like a withered monk.
translations.idiomatic: Born with a hidden physical defect, he had extraordinary stamina and would sit through the night leaning on a pillow like an ascetic monk.

sentences.zh: 內介而外和易。

translations.literal: Within he was upright; outwardly he was genial and easy.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly firm, outwardly genial.

sentences.zh: 論事謇諤，頗有聲公卿間云。

translations.literal: In discussing affairs he was forthright and outspoken; he had considerable reputation among the high ministers, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke bluntly on public affairs and enjoyed a strong reputation among senior officials.

sentences.zh: 沈家本，字子惇，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Shen Jiaben, style name Zidun, was a man of Gui'an, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiaben, whose style was Zidun, came from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少讀書，好深湛之思，於周官多創獲。

translations.literal: In youth he read books and delighted in deep, profound thought; on the Offices of Zhou he had many original gains.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved deep study and made many original insights into the Offices of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 初援例以郎中分刑部，博稽掌故，多所纂述。

translations.literal: At first, by precedent as a director he was assigned to the Ministry of Punishments; he broadly investigated precedents and compiled many works.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of Punishments by precedent as a director, researched precedents exhaustively, and compiled many works.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，成進士，仍留部。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu he completed the jinshi degree and still remained in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 he passed the jinshi examination and remained at the ministry.

sentences.zh: 補官後，充主稿，兼秋審處。

translations.literal: After filling his official post he served as chief drafter and concurrently in the Autumn Review Office.
translations.idiomatic: After regular appointment he served as chief drafter and also in the Autumn Review Office.

sentences.zh: 自此遂專心法律之學，爲尚書潘祖蔭所稱賞。

translations.literal: From this he then devoted himself to the study of law and was praised and appreciated by Minister Pan Zuyin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he devoted himself to legal studies and won the admiration of Minister Pan Zuyin.

sentences.zh: 十九年，出知天津府，治尚寬大，姦民易之，聚衆鬨於市，即擒斬四人，無敢復犯者。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he went out as prefect of Tianjin; his governance was still lenient and broad; wicked people took him lightly; a crowd made a disturbance in the market; he immediately seized and executed four men, and none dared offend again.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he became prefect of Tianjin. His rule was lenient, so ruffians took him lightly and rioted in the market; he seized and executed four ringleaders at once, and no one dared repeat the offense.

sentences.zh: 調劇保定，甘軍毀法國教堂，當路懾於外勢，償五萬金，以道署舊址建新堂，侵及府署東偏。

translations.literal: Transferred to the difficult post of Baoding, when Gansu troops destroyed a French church the authorities in power were awed by foreign force, paid fifty thousand taels of gold, and built a new church on the old site of the circuit office, encroaching on the eastern side of the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Baoding, he found that after Gansu troops had destroyed a French church the authorities, fearing foreign pressure, paid fifty thousand taels and planned a new church on the circuit yamen site, encroaching on the prefectural yamen.

sentences.zh: 家本據府志力爭得直。

translations.literal: Jiaben, relying on the prefectural gazetteer, strove forcefully and gained vindication.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaben cited the prefectural gazetteer and fought the case successfully.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂作，家本已擢通永道、山西按察使，未及行，兩宮西幸。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, Jiaben had already been promoted to Tongyong Circuit Intendant and Shanxi Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; before he could depart, the two palaces went west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out he had just been promoted to Tongyong circuit intendant and Shanxi surveillance commissioner but had not yet left office when the court fled west.

sentences.zh: 聯軍入保定，教士銜前隙，誣以助拳匪，卒無左驗而解。

translations.literal: When the allied armies entered Baoding, missionaries bore a prior grudge and falsely accused him of aiding the Boxers; in the end there was no corroborating evidence and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies entered Baoding, missionaries who bore old grudges accused him of aiding the Boxers, but with no evidence against him he was cleared.

sentences.zh: 因馳赴行在，授光祿寺卿，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he hurried to the traveling court, was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to the traveling court, was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 自各國互市以來，內地許傳教，而中外用律輕重懸殊，民、教日齟齬。

translations.literal: Since the various states began mutual trade, the interior was permitted missionary activity, yet Chinese and foreign application of law differed greatly in severity; commoners and missionaries daily clashed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the treaty ports opened, missionaries had been allowed inland, but Chinese and foreign law differed sharply in severity, and friction between commoners and missionaries grew daily.

sentences.zh: 官畏事則務抑民，民不能堪，則激而一逞，往往焚戮成巨禍。

translations.literal: Officials, fearing trouble, strove to suppress the people; when the people could not bear it they were provoked to one outburst, and often burning and slaughter became great calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, fearing trouble, suppressed the people; when the people could bear it no longer they erupted in violence, and great massacres often followed.

sentences.zh: 家本以謂治今日之民，當令官吏普通法律。

translations.literal: Jiaben held that to govern today's people, one should make officials thoroughly versed in law.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaben held that governing the people of today required making law common knowledge among officials.

sentences.zh: 然中律不變而欲收回領事審判權，終不可得。

translations.literal: Yet if Chinese law did not change and one wished to recover consular jurisdiction, in the end it could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet consular jurisdiction could never be recovered without reforming Chinese law itself.

sentences.zh: 會變法議起，袁世凱奏設修訂法律館，命家本偕伍廷芳總其事；

translations.literal: It happened that reform was discussed; Yuan Shikai memorialized to establish the Bureau for Revising the Laws and ordered Jiaben together with Wu Tingfang to take overall charge of its affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When reform was debated, Yuan Shikai proposed founding the Bureau for Revising the Laws and placed Jiaben and Wu Tingfang in joint charge;

sentences.zh: 別設法律學堂，畢業者近千人，一時稱盛。

translations.literal: A separate Law School was established; graduates approached a thousand; for a time it was called flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: A law school was also founded, producing nearly a thousand graduates in what was for a time a celebrated institution.

sentences.zh: 補大理寺卿，旋改法部侍郎，充修訂法律大臣。

translations.literal: He filled the post of President of the Court of Judicial Review, was shortly changed to Vice Minister of Law, and served as minister for revising the laws.
translations.idiomatic: He became president of the Court of Judicial Review, then Vice Minister of Law, and served as minister for legal revision.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，兼資政院副總裁，仍日與館員商訂諸法草案，先後告成，未嘗以事繁自解。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he concurrently served as vice president of the Political Consultative Council; still daily he discussed and fixed draft laws with bureau members; successively they were completed; he never excused himself on grounds of affairs being numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 he also served as vice president of the Political Consultative Council, yet still met daily with bureau staff to draft laws until the codes were completed, never pleading the press of business as an excuse.

sentences.zh: 其所著書，有讀律校勘記、秋讞須知、刑案匯覽、刺字集、律例偶箋、歷代刑官考、歷代刑法考、漢律摭遺、明大誥竣令考、明律目箋，他所著非刑律者又二十餘種，都二百餘卷。

translations.literal: His written works included Collation Notes on Reading the Code, Essentials of Autumn Review Cases, Compendium of Criminal Cases, Collection on Tattooing Marks, Occasional Notes on Statutes and Regulations, Study of Punishment Officials Through the Ages, Study of Punitive Law Through the Ages, Remnants of Han Law, Study of Ming Grand Admonitions and Completed Commands, and Commentary on Ming Code Headings; his other works not on penal law numbered more than twenty kinds, in all more than two hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Collation Notes on Reading the Code, Essentials of Autumn Review Cases, Compendium of Criminal Cases, Collection on Tattooing Marks, Occasional Notes on Statutes and Regulations, Studies of Punishment Officials and Punitive Law Through the Ages, Remnants of Han Law, studies of Ming admonitions and code headings, and more than twenty other non-penal works—over two hundred juan in all.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自變法議興，凡新政特設大臣領之。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: From the time reform was discussed, every new policy had a specially appointed great minister to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: Once reform was debated, every new policy was placed under a specially appointed minister.

sentences.zh: 百熙管學務，家本修法律，並邀時譽。

translations.literal: Baixi managed educational affairs, Jiaben revised the laws—both invited contemporary praise.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi directed education and Jiaben revised the laws, and both won contemporary acclaim.

sentences.zh: 景崇之主教育，謀溝通新舊；

translations.literal: Jingchong's heading of education sought to bridge old and new;
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong sought to reconcile old and new learning in education;

sentences.zh: 式枚之論憲政，務因時損益。

translations.literal: Shimei's discussion of constitutional government strove to adjust according to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei argued for constitutional government that would adjust institutions to the times.

sentences.zh: 而大勢所趨，已莫能挽救。

translations.literal: Yet the larger trend toward which matters moved could already not be rescued.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the tide of events was already beyond their power to reverse.

sentences.zh: 家鼐儒厚廉謹，常以資望領新政，每參大計，獨持正不阿。

translations.literal: Jianai was Confucian, generous, honest, and cautious; he often by senior standing led new policies; whenever he joined in great plans he alone upheld rectitude and did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: Jianai was scholarly, generous, and scrupulous; by senior standing he often headed new policies, and whenever he joined in great decisions he alone refused to trim his views.

sentences.zh: 賢哉，不愧古大臣矣！

translations.literal: How worthy! He does not fail to measure up to great ministers of old!
translations.idiomatic: Truly worthy—a minister in the ancient mold!
